ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening under PCMLTFA and FINTRAC guidance: (a) identify and verify all directors, officers, and individuals with significant control (UBOs) at the statutory 25% threshold; (b) determine whether any customer, beneficial owner, or authorized signatory is a foreign PEP, domestic PEP, or head of an international organization, and apply enhanced ongoing monitoring where any PEP designation is found; (c) screen all counterparties, investors, and payees against Canadian consolidated lists implemented under the United Nations Act, Special Economic Measures Act, and Criminal Code anti-terrorism listing (including the RCMP terrorist entity list and Global Affairs Canada consolidated SEMA list); (d) apply reasonable due diligence against U.S. OFAC SDN and sectoral listings wherever the fund clears through U.S. correspondent banks or transacts in USD; and (e) file FINTRAC reports as required, including terrorist property reports and reports on transactions involving listed persons. Failure to maintain a documented screening protocol constitutes a compliance deficiency subject to FINTRAC administrative monetary penalties and disqualifies the ULC from obtaining Canadian banking and payment-rail onboarding.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Registries and Online Services - 'Corporate Online' (https://www.bcregistry.gov.bc.ca, operated by the BC Registrar of Companies, Corporate and Land Registry, Ministry of Citizens' Services), including the consolidated oneStop Business Registry channel
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under s. 24 of the Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 57, and BC Reg. 64/2004, a corporate name must contain a distinctive element, a descriptive element, and a legal element; for an unlimited liability corporation the legal element must be 'Unlimited Liability Company', 'ULC', or the permitted French-language equivalents. Names must be submitted in Roman/Latin script; non-Roman business names must be transliterated to a recognizable Roman-script phonetic rendering. BC statutory naming doctrine requires that the name not be confusingly similar to an existing corporate, extra-provincial, or registered trade-mark name and that it not contain specific tokens triggering mandatory prior regulatory consent.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Institute (when implying a regulated educational institution)
Amalgamated (requires supporting statutory declaration of consolidation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the BC Corporate Online name-approval system issues a rejection, the applicant receives an electronic Name Request Rejection Notice identifying the objection (confusing similarity, non-distinctiveness, prohibited token, or misleading description). Administrative review: within 30 calendar days of rejection, the applicant files a written 'Name Review Request' to the Director of Name Approvals, BC Corporate Registry, supplying corrected tokens, consent letters from affected name or trade-mark holders, disclaimers, or additional distinguishing elements. The Registrar generally issues a second decision within 10-15 business days. If the administrative review is denied, the applicant may apply to the Supreme Court of British Columbia for judicial review under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 241, or may initiate a court application under the BCA contesting the Registrar's refusal. Alternatively, the applicant may file a fresh name request under a new transaction with a substantially revised distinctive element. No refund of the name-request fee is available on refusal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only where an in-province corporate services provider maintains a physical registered office and records office in British Columbia capable of accepting legal process and hosting the statutory records required under ss. 38-45 of the BCA. A pure postal-only virtual office with no service-capable physical BC address is non-compliant. For an ISIC 6499 revenue-based financing fund, BC registry law is satisfied through a virtual registered-agent office; however, Canadian Schedule I banks and FINTRAC-regulated payment processors will typically refuse account onboarding without a substantive operating address, and the Canada Revenue Agency may assert limited commercial substance or a deemed permanent establishment where management and control are exercised exclusively through the agent. Recommended architecture: virtual BC registered office plus an arm's-length Canadian fund administration agreement and a disclosed Canadian compliance officer to establish adequate commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified as low-to-moderate. The BC Registrar conducts office and records audits on a documentary basis; unannounced physical on-site inspection probability is estimated at below 5% annually per corporate file. CRA books-and-records examination and FINTRAC compliance examination risk for a non-deposit-taking royalty financing vehicle is approximately 10-15% annually, enhanced to approximately 20-25% where the ULC claims Canada-US treaty relief under Article XII for cross-border royalty-style payments, processes high-volume pre-authorized debits through Canadian payment rails, or maintains a U.S.-centric investor base with minimal Canadian board activity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (British Columbia), SBC 2002, c. 57, including sections 188-190 (incorporation by Notice of Articles and certificate), section 1(1) 'unlimited liability company', and the registered office, records office, director and officer provisions, together with the Business Corporations Regulation, B.C. Reg. 2/2004
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, BC Registries and Online Services, Ministry of Citizens' Services, Victoria, British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Articles and Incorporation Agreement, with Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement under the BC Business Corporations Act. A BC unlimited liability company (ULC) may issue no-par-value shares for such consideration as the directors determine; paid-up capital requirements arise only through the corporate agreements and tax elections, not through the Companies Act filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [●] UNLIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY, adopted by written consent. 1. Shares: The subscription of [●] common shares by the founding shareholder is approved. The directors determine that CAD [●] be paid by cash into the corporate bank account or as property acceptable to the board. 2. Registered Office: The registered office and records office of the corporation shall be [●], British Columbia. 3. Officers: [●] is appointed Chief Executive Officer, [●] Chief Financial Officer, and [●] Corporate Secretary, each to hold office until removed or the next annual meeting. 4. Administration: Officers are authorized to open bank accounts, engage legal counsel and accountants, and execute documents necessary to commence royalty financing operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name reservation and NUANS business name report
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services — Corporate Name Request module (bcregistries.ca)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access BC Registries Online and submit 1-3 proposed names with the mandatory ULC suffix, e.g. '[●] Unlimited Liability Company' or '[●] ULC'. The name request is queued for examination; after approval, retain the name request number for the incorporation filing. A name approval is generally valid for 56 days. Use the name report to confirm the name is distinguishable from existing BC corporate names.
required_dossiers: Name search or NUANS report, if requested
Applicant contact details and name request payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name request is refused, file a new name request with alternative names, request reconsideration with the Registrar, or add a distinguishing element. No fee refund is made, but the name request queue permits rapid resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting Notice of Articles and ULC incorporation agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company legal counsel or incorporator preparing the BC Corporate Online filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Notice of Articles and Incorporation Agreement. State expressly that the company is an unlimited liability company, adopt the 'ULC' tag, define an authorized capital structure of no-par-value shares, name the first directors, and set the initial registered and records office address in British Columbia. Execute the Incorporation Agreement and obtain each director's written consent to act.
required_dossiers: Incorporation Agreement executed by the incorporator or shareholder
Consent to act as director for each first director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query, revise the inconsistent provisions, re-execute the agreement where necessary, and refile before the name reservation expires. Counsel should confirm the tag 'Unlimited Liability Company' is used consistently in all drafts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of incorporation and issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, BC Registries and Online Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to BC Corporate Online, submit the Notice of Articles, and pay the statutory filing fee. The Registrar examines the notice, registers the company, and issues a Certificate of Incorporation. The company comes into existence on the date stated in the certificate. Download the Certificate of Incorporation from BC Corporate Online for all subsequent banking, tax, and licensing steps.
required_dossiers: Payment confirmation from BC Corporate Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is rejected, correct the defective Notice of Articles and refile. If the Registry issues a request for further information, respond within the stated deadline through BC Corporate Online and supplement the docket with the requested corporate records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First board resolutions, share subscription, registered office, and officer appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors acting by written resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the first board resolution by written consent of all directors. Approve the allotment and issuance of founding common shares upon receipt of subscription consideration, confirm the registered office and records office in British Columbia, appoint the Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary, and authorize officers to open bank accounts and execute agreements necessary for royalty financing operations.
required_dossiers: Signed First Board Resolution / written consent
Share subscription agreement and payment evidence
Corporate records book, share register, and records office register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director or officer becomes unavailable, pass a substitute appointment resolution and file the required Notice of Change of Directors or officers with BC Registries, accompanied by the new consent to act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA business number and tax account registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency — Business Registration Online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the Certificate of Incorporation and corporate details to register for a federal business number (BN). Activate the corporate income tax account, register for GST/HST where required, and open a payroll deduction account if employees are engaged. For a BC ULC operating as a royalty financing fund, confirm all permanent establishments are disclosed and maintain English-language corporate records for CRA compliance.
required_dossiers: Business address and principal place of business in Canada
Director identification information and corporate bank account details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the BN is delayed or rejected, contact the CRA Business Window or use Represent a Client to submit the Certificate of Incorporation and first board resolution as validating evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal business licence and physical premises occupancy clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal planning and licensing department, local fire authority, and WorkSafeBC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal business licence for the physical operating office. Obtain an occupancy permit for the registered premises and arrange a fire safety inspection where the premises are occupied. Because the royalty financing fund conducts only administrative and financial office operations, no industrial manufacturing or processing equipment is installed. Confirm with the municipality that the use is 'financial services office' and not a regulated industrial use.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or proof of legal premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality issues an occupancy or zoning violation, submit a corrected floor plan, proof of fire safety remediation, and any required zoning variance application. If the business licence is refused, petition the municipal licensing committee and provide the certificate of incorporation and lease as supporting documents.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal Planning and Development Department and Local Fire Authority for the physical office; no sectoral industrial licence is required under BC Financial Services Authority for a non-deposit, non-lending royalty financing fund classified under ISIC 6499
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Licence and Occupancy Permit (non-industrial financial services office)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy — Environmental Assessment Office
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full environmental impact assessment; the operation is an administrative office with no designated project under the BC Environmental Assessment Act and no industrial activity trigger.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, volatile organic compounds, or combustion emissions are generated by royalty financing administration. Office waste must be disposed through municipal collection; electronic waste and batteries must be handled under the BC Hazardous Waste Regulation and municipal e-waste programs. If a standby generator is installed, it must meet local air emission and fire code thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Occupancy permit from the local building authority, fire safety certification from the local fire department, structural load approval for office floor use, and WorkSafeBC workplace compliance clearance including emergency exits, evacuation plan, and ergonomic workstation assessment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency / Agence du revenu du Canada (CRA/ARC); business registration portal: https://www.canada.ca/en/services/taxes/business.html
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: After incorporating the BC ULC under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia), register for a federal Business Number with CRA through Business Registration Online or by filing Form RC1. Select program accounts for corporate income tax (RC) and GST/HST (RT); non-resident corporations may also need a non-resident T2 return profile. CRA issues a 9-digit BN plus program account suffix that serves as the tax identity (TIN/VAT ID) for federal filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (for Canadian federal and BC income tax purposes a ULC is a taxable corporation filing T2; foreign jurisdictions may classify it as a pass-through entity via check-the-box election, but that election does not alter Canadian domestic treatment)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No domestic check-the-box election exists under the Canadian Income Tax Act; the BC ULC is mandatorily taxed as a corporation. For U.S. federal tax purposes, eligible taxpayers may file Form 8832 to elect disregarded-entity or partnership classification. Canadian hybrid-mismatch rules apply to cross-border arrangements involving such entity classification differences and may recharacterise or deny deductions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) plus British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST) — dual indirect tax system
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 in taxable supplies over the immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters for GST/HST; BC PST requires registration upon first taxable sale, with a limited small-seller exemption for sellers whose BC taxable sales are below C$10,000 in the prior 12 months.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory API e-invoicing system. GST/HST e-invoicing is permitted but voluntary; CRA requires records to be retained in readable electronic or paper form and that GST/HST invoices show prescribed particulars (supplier BN/RT number, date, description, consideration and tax). Pan-Canadian PEPPOL-based e-invoicing is carried out on a voluntary basis.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: To claim 0% GST/HST on an export, the registrant must make a qualifying supply under Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act. For goods, the goods must be exported from Canada in accordance with CRA/CBSA requirements and the registrant must maintain evidence of export. For services, intangibles or licence/royalty supplies, the recipient must be a non-resident not registered for GST/HST, the supply must not be for consumption/use in Canada, and it must not relate to real property situated in Canada. Financial services supplied by a royalty-financing fund are generally exempt, not zero-rated; where an exempt financial supply is made to a non-resident for use wholly outside Canada, the fund cannot recover input tax credits on related exempt supplies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (B13A) or approved electronic export reporting through CBSA
Carrier-issued Bill of Lading or air waybill showing movement from Canada to foreign destination (for services/intangibles: contract, licence agreement, and delivery records)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT/foreign-exchange record evidencing repatriation of export proceeds
Commercial invoice and zero-rated GST/HST invoice identifying the non-resident recipient, description, consideration and supplier BN/RT account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may deny zero-rating and retroactively assess GST/HST, interest and penalties if export conditions or documentary requirements are not satisfied within prescribed time limits. False or misleading statements in GST/HST filings attract penalties under the Excise Tax Act (up to 25% of the amount involved for false statements), plus gross-negligence penalties of 50% of understated income tax under the Income Tax Act s. 163(2) for intentional cases. Fraudulent zero-rating schemes may be subject to criminal prosecution and director liability, and BC PST audits can claw back uncollected provincial sales tax with interest and administrative penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); monetary authority and sole issuer of Canadian bank notes. There is no dedicated Foreign Exchange Administration in Canada. FX and capital-movement policy sits with the Department of Finance Canada under the Currency Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. C-52). Prudential oversight of FX activities of banks and authorized foreign banks lies with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) under the Bank Act and OSFI Guideline B-13. Transaction-level anti-money-laundering reporting (international electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more) is enforced by FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). Payment-clearing system oversight is performed by Payments Canada under the Canadian Payments Act, with the Bank of Canada operating wholesale settlement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: CAD is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts. Canada has had a free-floating exchange rate since 1970 and abolished exchange controls in 1951; no Canadian approval is required to convert CAD, to hold USD or EUR, to receive foreign currency, or to remit dividends, interest, or royalties abroad. Profit-repatriation constraints are purely tax-driven: dividends paid by a BC ULC to non-resident shareholders attract Part XIII withholding tax (statutory 25%; treaty-reduced to 15% for portfolio US dividends and 5% for a US shareholder owning at least 10% of voting shares under Article X of the Canada-US Tax Convention). Interest paid at arm's length on non-participating debt is withholding-exempt (paragraph 212(1)(b)). Royalty payments to US residents are subject to a statutory 25% withholding with a 10% treaty rate under Article XII, unless the narrow copyright-royalty exception applies. As the ULC is eligible for pass-through tax treatment but is a Canadian resident under the treaty, the Canada-US protocol hybrid-entity rules must be verified to avoid double taxation or treaty-shopping denial. No exchange controls apply to repatriation of the royalty-financing fund's Canadian-source profits; only ordinary reporting of year-end foreign assets to Form T1135 is required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada does not require export goods, services, or royalty proceeds to be surrendered, and there is no statutory timeline for their repatriation and no mandatory conversion ratio. Revenue-based financing receivables denominated in USD may be kept in US-dollar operating accounts or held offshore. The only binding obligations are FINTRAC reporting requirements (any international EFT of CAD 10,000 or more must be reported by the financial entity; physical cross-border movement of currency or monetary instruments of CAD 10,000 or more must be declared to the Canada Border Services Agency) and the foreign-property reporting obligation of Form T1135 if the aggregate cost amount of the ULC's specified foreign property exceeds CAD 100,000 at any time in the taxation year.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for borrower collateral and repayment sweeps
Payment Clearing Account with US-domiciled ACH routing via BMO Harris
Treasury and trade-finance account (LC issuance and MT103 settlement)
Regional operational account for West-coast borrower disbursements

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium as an ancillary liquidity channel; not acceptable as the primary treasury bank. Legal constraints: Canada has no EMI passporting regime equivalent to the EU, so licences held by UK/EU EMIs (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer) do not confer Canadian bank status, and funds held with such EMIs are not CDIC-insured. The ULC may lawfully maintain an offshore EMI account, but the balance triggers Form T1135 filing when aggregate foreign property exceeds CAD 100,000; the EMI is outside the OSFI supervisory perimeter and cannot issue a Canadian-domiciled account number usable for Canadian ACH debit origination. If the EMI provides third-party payment processing for the ULC's merchant disbursements, the ULC's primary bank will treat the EMI as a third-party payment processor (TPPP) and may require dual accounts, daily cash-flow reconciliation, and contractual indemnities. The ULC should not provide money-transfer services through EMIs unless it is registered as a Money Service Business with FINTRAC under the PCMLTFA; a crypto or remittance component would trigger that registration.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical, in-branch KYC interview will be required for at least one director or a designated corporate officer of the ULC. Canadian Schedule I banks classify newly incorporated BC ULCs engaged in non-dilutive revenue-based financing as Medium_Risk_Enhanced; consequently, remote-only onboarding is generally rejected. Recommended onboarding path: (1) appoint a BC-resident director or engage a licensed corporate services agent; (2) book an interview at the bank's Vancouver Financial Centre; (3) bring original passports, the certificate of incorporation, the ULC's articles and notice of articles, the register of directors, and a certified board resolution; (4) provide notarized ID and proof of address for each 25% or greater beneficial owner. RBC and BMO operate limited remote-capture pilots, but only for low-risk, pre-vetted relationships; a pure video-KYC close will not achieve sign-off for a royalty-financing fund in the absence of Canadian legal counsel acting as a KYC conduit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity in the hybrid US/Canada ownership chain of the ULC and the non-linear 25% UBO threshold
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate charters and share registry from the BC Corporate Registry; an ownership waterfall chart; source-of-funds evidence (12 months of brokerage/bank statements) for each UBO; FATCA/CRS self-certifications (Form W-8BEN-E for US owners, Form NR301 for Canadian residents); and a Canadian tax opinion confirming that the ULC is the beneficial owner of the royalty-financing receivables.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unlicensed-lending appearance of ISIC 6499 / NAICS 525990 activities without a financial-services licence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: BC legal memorandum confirming the commercial-lending exemption from the Business Practices and Consumer Protection Act (BPCPA); structural loan documents including master financing agreement, revenue-share notes, and UCC-1 filings; fund financial statements; a securities-law opinion that the revenue-based financing instruments are not investment contracts under the BC Securities Act; and confirmation that no BCFSA mortgage-brokerage or payday-lending licence is engaged.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume digital-merchant disbursements with early settlement and instant-payout features flagged as potential money-laundering or credit-fraud vectors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant onboarding and verification policy; a redacted merchant roster with country and sector spread; third-party operational audits of the disbursement platform; chargeback and refund procedures; a sanctions and PEP screening protocol; and monthly negative-news screening logs to be shared with the bank for the first twelve months.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Classic yield-stripping or hybrid-mismatch pattern in an Unlimited Liability Corporation with cross-border US shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A substance report evidencing management and decision-making in British Columbia (leases, payroll, tax remittances); transfer-pricing documentation for intercompany financing and royalty flows (Canada-US Form T106 and Schedule 7); a ULC pass-through election analysis under subsection 34.1(2.3) of the Income Tax Act if applicable; and an international-tax opinion addressing the Canada-US protocol fiscally-transparent rule to prevent treaty denial.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lump-sum inbound equity contribution from a single US brokerage account triggering IEFT and source-of-funds scrutiny
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Escrow or attorney closing letter; complete wire chain; executed share-subscription agreements; a source-of-wealth letter from the remitting institution; the investor's personal tax filings or audited statements; and the bank's Large-Value Funds Transfer questionnaire completed with a reconciliation of the contribution to the ULC's opening balance sheet.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Design the inbound leg as SWIFT-based CAD wires to the ULC's operating account at a Schedule I bank, using ISO 20022 purpose code NGIN (non-resident investment in domestic entities). For USD-denominated injections, direct the wire to the ULC's USD correspondent account with RBC (SWIFT BIC ROYCCAT2) or TD (BIC TDOMCATTTOR), and execute a same-day FX conversion to CAD at the account bank. Every injection requires a share-subscription agreement, CRS/FATCA self-certification, updated registers, and pre-notification to FINTRAC via the bank's IEFT report; inbound investments exceeding CAD 10,000 are automatically reported, and the bank may request a Funds Transfer Declaration. The ULC must also deliver the Investment Canada Act form F-1 (notification of establishment of a new Canadian business) to the Federal Minister of Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada within 30 days of establishment; the initial capital will be far below the 2025 net-benefit review threshold. If a related US party funds the contribution, include an opinion that the payment is equity, that it cannot be recharacterized as back-to-back debt, and that the ULC's interest deductibility is not limited by the EIFEL rule in subsection 18.2(4) of the Income Tax Act if the financing-entity exclusion applies.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For merchant advances and trade settlements above CAD 50,000, use a SWIFT MT103 through the bank's New York correspondent, with beneficiary account, ABA or CHIPS routing, and a 72-character narrative citing the merchant contract and invoice number. For routine revenue-sharing disbursements below CAD 50,000 to US merchants, use NACHA ACH through the Canadian bank's US bank affiliate (e.g., BMO Harris or TD Bank, N.A.) with SEC code WEB; Canadian merchants are funded through the Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) or the future Real-Time Rail (RTR) instant-payment system, with pre-authorized debits (PADs) originated under Canadian Payments Act Rule H1. The fund's monthly repayments from merchants are collected via the same rails: PAD for Canadian debits and US ACH debit conversion; negative debit-blocking and returns must be monitored daily. For cross-border equipment or content-vendor imports, open a commercial letter-of-credit facility with CIBC or BMO under UCP600 using a 30-90 day deferred-payment tenor. All outbound payments of CAD 10,000 or more are IEFT-reportable; the ULC must avoid payment structuring or smurfing, and the treasury policy will reject cash disbursements entirely.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CAD/USD vanilla FX forward contracts (tenor up to 24 months) transparently hedging underlying royalty-financing receivables and loan disbursements
Cross-currency swaps converting USD floating-rate exposure into CAD fixed-rate obligations, executed under the British Columbia Derivatives Act end-user exemption and an ISDA 2002 master agreement
FX rolling swaps for daily CAD/USD conversion inherent in the fund's cash-sweep engine, with same-day settlement in the bank's nostro accounts
Vanilla European-style FX options (CAD/USD and CAD/EUR, premium-paid only, no written naked options) to cap conversion volatility on the aggregate quarterly repayment pools

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) or deliverable FX swaps in less-convertible merchant currencies (e.g., BRL, INR, TRY, PHP) solely where an ISDA-cleared onshore deliverable market is unavailable and the underlying revenue-sharing receivables are denominated in those currencies
Incidental interest-rate swaps on the fund's US private-credit liability, subject to staggered maturity guidance and the EIFEL limitation in subsection 18.2 of the Income Tax Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registrar of Companies, BC Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the anniversary date of incorporation; a late filing fee may be paid for up to two months after the anniversary; thereafter the registrar may issue notice of impending administrative dissolution.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of CAD 100 (approx. USD 75) after the anniversary date; continued non-filing within the registrar's notice period may result in administrative strike-off, loss of corporate powers, and director personal risk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal, including financial statement schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; tax payable is due two months after fiscal year-end, or three months after fiscal year-end for certain Canadian-controlled private corporations eligible for late remittance.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty under section 162 of the Income Tax Act is 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month of delinquency up to 12 months; repeated failure to file may trigger additional penalties of 10% or more, director liability, and possible CRA tax audit.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A private BC unlimited liability corporation is not statutorily required to undergo an external audit solely on the basis of revenue or asset thresholds under the BC Business Corporations Act; an audit becomes mandatory if the articles or unanimous shareholder agreement require it, if shareholders holding at least 5% of the issued shares demand one, or if the company is a reporting issuer. Lenders or investors in royalty-financing structures commonly impose audit covenants as a contractual trigger.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; private BC ULCs may use Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook unless a stakeholder or regulator requires IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the BC Business Corporations Act, the company must maintain a transparency register of significant individuals (beneficial owners) and update it within 60 days of any share transfer or change in significant control. No separate annual UBO filing is submitted to the BC Registrar; the annual report confirms director changes and registered office only. The transparency register must be made available to enforcement authorities on demand but is not a public registry.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - 18,000 per year for a small private ULC engaged in royalty-based financing, with higher ranges for complex cross-border or fund-like structures

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal general corporate rate 15% plus British Columbia general corporate rate 12%, yielding an aggregate headline rate of 27% before any provincial abatement. A BC Unlimited Liability Corporation is a Canadian resident taxpayer subject to tax on worldwide income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday applies to ISIC 6499. Available incentives include the Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credit (15% federal non-refundable, refundable 35% on first CAD 3 million of eligible expenditures for qualified Canadian-controlled private corporations); the BC small business rate of 2% combined with the federal 9% small business rate (11% aggregate) on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income if the ULC is a CCPC; and accelerated capital cost allowance for certain eligible intellectual property. The ULC's possible US check-the-box pass-through election does not alter Canadian corporate taxation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return and T2 Schedule 5 (BC provincial tax), filed electronically with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) using the CRA Corporation Internet Filing portal or an approved E-file service provider. BC corporate tax is collected by the CRA under the federal-provincial tax collection agreement.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T2 return is due within 6 months after the end of the fiscal period; for a December 31 year-end, the filing deadline is June 30 of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report all gross business revenue from revenue-based financing, including royalty receipts, financing fees, interest income, and revenue from Canadian and foreign licensees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a ULC with non-resident owners, include all Canadian-source income attributed to the Canadian permanent establishment; foreign-source business income may be reported on Schedule 91 with residual taxes deductible under s.126.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 120 - Net Income (Loss) for Tax Purposes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct ordinary business expenses such as interest on acquisition financing, amortization of royalty/financing intellectual property, legal and professional fees, allowances for doubtful revenue-based contracts, and arm's-length royalty fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be reasonable and equivalent to what an arm's-length person would pay; amounts paid to non-resident shareholders beyond an arm's-length rate are subject to s.247(2) recharacterization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply available non-capital loss carryovers, capital gains/losses (schedules 6 and 7), and treaty-based deductions to determine combined federal/provincial taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify that the ULC maintains a physical permanent establishment, active bank/advisor services in BC, and records of director decisions; a paper-only entity may have its taxable income redetermined by CRA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate BC corporate income tax using the BC allocation formula (permanent establishment basis) and claim the BC small business deduction if eligible.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ULCs filing under Part I must ensure the head office and management are in BC; extra-provincial registration with BC Corporate Registry does not by itself create allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form T106 - Aggregate Reportable Non-Arm's-Length Transactions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report intercompany transactions with non-resident related parties, including royalty payments from foreign operating companies, revenue-sharing payments from licensees, loans advanced to the fund, and interest/guarantee fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File a separate T106 schedule for each non-resident non-arm's-length party with transactions exceeding CAD 1,000,000; state the transfer pricing method used (e.g., TNMM) and attach contemporaneous documentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file a T2 return triggers an automatic penalty of 5% of unpaid balance, plus 1% per full month of delay up to 12 months; gross negligence penalties are 50% of any misstatement. Failure to file Form T106 attracts CAD 100 per day (minimum CAD 1,000, maximum CAD 2,500). Late payment interest is compound at the CRA prescribed rate.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII withholding tax on dividends paid or credited to a non-resident person from Canadian sources, absent treaty relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For an investor resident in a treaty country (e.g., the United States), the non-resident must submit a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) or equivalent (for the US, IRS Form 6166) and CRA Form NR301/NR302 to the Canadian payer; the payer separates treaty and non-treaty residents, withholds the reduced rate, and files the Part XIII remittance with the CRA. The entitlement to treaty benefits must be supported by economic substance, and CRA may require a post-assessment review of the beneficial ownership through conduits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rate is 25% for interest and 25% for royalty payments. Under the Canada-US Income Tax Convention, arm's-length interest is generally exempt from Canadian withholding, and royalty withholding is reduced to 10% (0% for certain software copyright royalties). A reduction is unavailable if the recipient is not the beneficial owner or if the amount exceeds an arm's-length consideration.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 aggregate non-arm's-length transactions with any one non-resident party per taxation year, triggering Form T106 and contemporaneous Local File; Master File and Country-by-Country Report may be required for multinational groups with consolidated revenue exceeding CAD 100,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has not enacted Economic Substance Regulations of the UAE/OECD type; however, the general anti-avoidance rule (ITA s.245), the beneficial ownership doctrine, and OECD BEPS recommendations permit the CRA to disregard or recharacterize a royalty financing ULC that lacks real management, employees, material risks, or economic activities in BC. CRA may defer to economic substance when applying intercompany financing and treaty anti-abuse provisions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly signing a false T2 return, suppressing royalty/revenue income, creating fictitious financing expenses, or moving revenue to a shell ULC with no actual operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Conviction under ITA s.239 carries a fine of 50% to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years; civil consequences include a 50% gross-negligence penalty, compound arrears interest, and re-opening of the statute-barred years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who direct or knowingly participate in evasion can be prosecuted as parties, subjected to restitution, personal monetary penalties, asset seizure, and a travel ban pending proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare contemporaneous TP documentation or file Form T106 for intercompany royalty loans above the CAD 1,000,000 threshold, or using a pricing methodology inconsistent with arm's-length principles.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under ITA s.247(3), a penalty of 10% of the net transfer-pricing adjustment is imposed; additional late T106 penalties of CAD 100 per day (max CAD 2,500) apply; CRA reassesses and charges prescribed interest on adjusted amounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors knowingly signing false T106 or approving fictitious intercompany prices may be jointly liable for the assessed penalties and subject to criminal charges under s.239 if wilful.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a BC ULC with no staff, no Canadian board meetings, no premises or risk, and using it merely as a conduit for royalty/financing income to a tax-haven parent while claiming treaty reductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may invoke the GAAR to deny treaty benefits, treat the ULC as a sham for tax purposes, assess Part XIII at 25% on undeclared distributions, and apply transfer-pricing penalties; the BC Business Corporations Act may strike the company for non-compliance with registered-records requirements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly operate a conduit can be personally assessed for withholding liabilities under s.227.1, named in civil recovery proceedings, and barred from re-entering Canada if criminal tax evasion is alleged.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the revenue-based financing fund to launder proceeds of crime, failing to register as a money-services business under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), failing to file suspicious transaction reports with FINTRAC, or structuring wire transfers to evade reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FINTRAC administrative penalties up to CAD 500,000 per corporation and CAD 100,000 per individual; criminal money laundering under Criminal Code s.462.31 is an indictable offense punishable by up to 10 years imprisonment and full asset confiscation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers with knowledge of, or wilful blindness to, laundering face personal prosecution, forfeiture orders, imprisonment, and can be subjected to travel bans and asset freezes during the criminal investigation.
